claim: AAAI 2026 received 23,680 submissions and accepted 4,167 papers, a 17.6% acceptance rate, the lowest in three years — the concrete numeric bar DPRC-as-AAAI-27 must clear.
stance_target: quantitative competitiveness of the AAAI main-track bar
quoted_support: With a record 23,680 submissions and 4,167 AAAI 2026 accepted papers, the 17.6% acceptance rate marks the lowest in three years.

claim: AAAI 2026's AI-assisted review pipeline explicitly scores submissions on five dimensions — Story, Presentation, Evaluations (baselines/test sets/significance tests/reproducibility), Correctness, and Significance/novelty — giving a concrete rubric DPRC will be judged against.
stance_target: what dimensions AAAI reviewers/AI-reviewers explicitly evaluate
scope_conditions: AAAI-26 AI Review Pilot, 22,977 main-track submissions
quoted_support: Independent agents inspect the paper along five dimensions: Story ... Presentation ... Evaluations: baselines, test sets, significance tests, reproducibility ... Correctness ... Significance: novelty and positioning

claim: AI reviewers at AAAI-26 outperformed human reviewers most on 'spotting deep technical errors' (+0.67) and 'surfacing counter-evidence the authors missed' (+0.61), meaning weak experimental claims are increasingly likely to be caught.
stance_target: increased scrutiny risk for under-evidenced claims (e.g., DPRC's single-model, small-benchmark result)
scope_conditions: 5,834 survey responses across AAAI-26 authors and PC members, 5-point Likert scale
quoted_support: Spotting deep technical errors +0.67 ... Surfacing counter-evidence the authors missed +0.61

claim: COREA (an SLM/LLM confidence-cascade system) is cited by this blog as an AAAI 2026 accepted paper achieving ~21.5% inference-cost reduction on out-of-domain math datasets while staying within 2% absolute pass@1 of LLM-only performance — but this venue attribution conflicts with the arXiv page's own comment of 'Accepted to EACL 2026 Main Conference.'
stance_target: venue accuracy of secondary-source AAAI paper lists; also a comparable confidence-calibration + downstream-utility framing example
scope_conditions: confidence-calibrated SLM-LLM cascade, math and non-math reasoning datasets
quoted_support: The result: ~21.5% inference cost reduction on out-of-domain math datasets while staying within 2% of LLM-only performance.

claim: A cross-conference macro trend at AAAI 2026 is 'From Scaling to Efficiency' — papers rewarded for smart architecture and inference-time computation beating brute-force scale, exemplified by small models that defer to large ones only when uncertain (COREA) and small models outperforming large ones via structured search (JUPITER).
stance_target: what framing narrative is currently rewarded at AAAI for confidence/uncertainty-adjacent contributions
scope_conditions: AAAI 2026 accepted-paper trend synthesis across multiple papers
quoted_support: The era of "bigger is always better" is fading. Papers like COREA (small models deferring to large ones only when uncertain) ... all point in the same direction: smart architecture and inference-time computation beat brute-force scale.

claim: AI reviewers at AAAI-26 underperformed human reviewers on 'big-picture judgment' — recognizing paradigm-shifting work or long-term scientific impact — meaning novelty framing still needs to persuade human ACs, not just pass automated evaluation checks.
stance_target: residual importance of narrative/framing quality for AAAI acceptance despite AI-assisted review
scope_conditions: open-ended feedback clustering from AAAI-26 review pilot
quoted_support: Big-picture judgment (9.1% of negative comments) — AI struggles to recognize paradigm-shifting work or rate long-term scientific impact.
